cl-hamlet-primary.title: William Shakespeare, Hamlet, Folger Shakespeare Library reading edition
cl-hamlet-primary.notes: Modern edited, sometimes conflated reading text. Folger flags the textual witnesses and variants.

cl-hamlet-folger-texts.title: Folger Shakespeare Library, Hamlet textual history and early print witnesses
cl-hamlet-folger-texts.notes: First Quarto 1603; Second Quarto 1604/1605; First Folio 1623. Competing readings.

cl-hamlet-folger-critical.title: Folger Shakespeare Library, Hamlet: A Modern Perspective
cl-hamlet-folger-critical.notes: Revenge plot, doubts, performance and sources; interpretive perspective, not direct authorial intent.

cl-hamlet-rsc-plot.title: Royal Shakespeare Company, Hamlet plot and key moments
cl-hamlet-rsc-plot.notes: Independent outline of major plot beats and staging decisions.

cl-hamlet-rsc-sources.title: Royal Shakespeare Company, Hamlet: dates and sources
cl-hamlet-rsc-sources.notes: Composition circa 1600–1601 and earlier Amleth, Saxo, Belleforest and lost play.

cl-hamlet-ophelia.title: Two Shakespearean Suicides, Essays in Criticism, 2022
cl-hamlet-ophelia.notes: Interpretive discussion of the ambiguity of Ophelia’s drowning and burial; consulted source description.

cl-quixote-primary-es.title: Miguel de Cervantes, Don Quijote de la Mancha, Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes
cl-quixote-primary-es.notes: Spanish primary text in a later scholarly edition; includes both parts. Not exhaustive line-by-line collation.

cl-quixote-primary-en.title: Don Quixote (1605, 1615), John Ormsby public-domain English translation, Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes
cl-quixote-primary-en.notes: Chapter-level English text; translation is a particular witness, not the source of an English original.

cl-quixote-bne.title: Biblioteca Nacional de España, Quijotes collections and original editions
cl-quixote-bne.notes: First printings 1605 and 1615, later editions and translations.

cl-quixote-bvc-first.title: Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes, digital facsimile of 1605 first printing
cl-quixote-bvc-first.notes: Catalog and images of Spanish first edition printed by Juan de la Cuesta.

cl-quixote-bvc-second.title: Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes, digital facsimile of 1615 second part
cl-quixote-bvc-second.notes: Catalog and images of Part II printed by Juan de la Cuesta.

cl-quixote-glasgow.title: University of Glasgow Library Special Collections, Hispanica: Literary Works
cl-quixote-glasgow.notes: 1605/1615 copies, reprints, misplaced Sancho donkey material, 1612 Shelton English translation and 1614 Avellaneda sequel.

cl-quixote-close.title: Anthony J. Close, The legacy of Don Quijote and the picaresque novel, Cambridge Companion to the Spanish Novel
cl-quixote-close.notes: Contexts Cervantes in older romance and picaresque; only abstract/preview directly available.

cl-dante-princeton-text.title: Princeton Dante Project, Commedia and canto browser
cl-dante-princeton-text.notes: English/Italian facing text and scholarly commentary interface; Giorgio Petrocchi base Italian text. Not redistributed.

cl-dante-world-of-dante.title: University of Virginia, World of Dante
cl-dante-world-of-dante.notes: University instructional digital edition, canto geography, searchable Italian and English text, and context for the three cantiche.

cl-dante-dartmouth-lab.title: Dartmouth Dante Lab, reading and scholarly commentary
cl-dante-dartmouth-lab.notes: Multi-century commentary tradition and textual comparison tool; different interpretations must not be treated as one consensus.

cl-dante-dartmouth-faq.title: Dante Lab: FAQ and editions
cl-dante-dartmouth-faq.notes: Identifies Petrocchi-based Italian text and Longfellow English text; redistribution of Petrocchi material is restricted.

cl-dante-leeds-paradiso.title: University of Leeds, Paradiso: Moon, Mercury, Venus
cl-dante-leeds-paradiso.notes: Canto II–IX outlines and scholarly treatment of Piccarda, vows, and representations of beatitude.

cl-dante-stanford-encyclopedia.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Dante Alighieri
cl-dante-stanford-encyclopedia.notes: Biographical, philosophical and political context; Florence and 1302 exile; distinguishes the author's project from pure theology.

cl-dante-cambridge-chronology.title: Cambridge Companion to Dante, second edition, chronology
cl-dante-cambridge-chronology.notes: Historical timeline through Dante’s lifetime, including 1300 journey setting and 1302 exile.

cl-dante-cambridge-narrative.title: Cambridge Companion to Dante's Commedia, Narrative Structure
cl-dante-cambridge-narrative.notes: Contrasts narrative organization and imagery across realms; scholarly perspective rather than sole interpretive authority.

cl-dante-cornell-manuscript.title: Cornell University Library, Dante from Manuscript to Printed Book
cl-dante-cornell-manuscript.notes: No authorial autograph; extensive surviving manuscript tradition; early printed and illustrated editions.

cl-dante-cornell-foligno.title: Cornell University Library, Incunables as Books of Transition
cl-dante-cornell-foligno.notes: Identifies Foligno 1472 as first printed edition and its role in the dissemination of Dante.

cl-dante-cambridge-transmission.title: Cambridge University Press, Dante in Context: Textual Transmission
cl-dante-cambridge-transmission.notes: No surviving autograph; surviving variants and editorial reconstructions, with interpretive limits.

cl-dante-princeton-title.title: Princeton Dante Project, Toynbee on the title 'Comedìa'
cl-dante-princeton-title.notes: Distinguishes medieval title forms from later use of Divina Commedia; 1555 Venetian printed title.

cl-dante-boccaccio-public-readings.title: Catherine Keen, Dante's Fortuna (UCL institutional repository)
cl-dante-boccaccio-public-readings.notes: Boccaccio's October 1373 publicly funded Florentine Dante lectures and the rise of formal public commentary.

cl-dante-gutenberg-longfellow.title: Project Gutenberg, Divine Comedy, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow translation
cl-dante-gutenberg-longfellow.notes: Public-domain English translation, 1867; useful for comparison with modern versions, not equivalent to Italian original.
